identity.title: Singly and doubly deuterated formaldehyde in massive star-forming regions

paper_type_evidence.quote: Using the APEX SEPIA Band 5 receiver, we extended our pilot study of the $J$=3$\rightarrow$2 rotational lines of HDCO and D$_2$CO to eleven high-mass star-forming regions that host objects at different evolutionary stages.
In this paper, we use the continuum and H$_2^{13}$CO emission information at 213 GHz to derive the source sizes.

question.value: Whether the deuteration fraction of formaldehyde (HDCO/H2CO, D2CO/HDCO) in high-mass star-forming cores can be used as an evolutionary tracer from HMSC to HMPO to UC HII stages

evidence.quote: In this paper we study the deuteration fraction of formaldehyde in high-mass star-forming cores at different evolutionary stages to investigate whether the deuteration fraction of formaldehyde can be used as an evolutionary tracer.
We performed high-resolution single pointing observations with ALMA in Cycle 5 as part of the 2017.1.01157.S project (PI: S. Zahorecz).

evidence.quote: Band 6 observations were executed for G028-C1, G34-F2, G34-G2, 18089-1732, 18517+0437, G5.89-0.39, I1935-VLA1 and 1941+2336.

evidence.quote: We used two setups to observe selected molecular lines, including H$_2^{13}$CO, and to observe the continuum emission.
In this paper, we use the continuum and H$_2^{13}$CO emission information at 213 GHz to derive the source sizes.

claims.hypothesis: Does the H2CO deuteration fraction decrease with evolutionary stage in high-mass star-forming regions?
claims.experiment: APEX SEPIA HDCO and D2CO spectra of 11 sources with IRAM H2CO data, LTE fits with MADCUBA, source sizes from ALMA continuum
claims.result: HDCO/H2CO falls from ~0.13 in early HMPO phases to ~0.01 in UC HII regions
claims.finding: The deuteration fraction of formaldehyde decreases with evolutionary stage

evidence.quote: the deuteration fraction of formaldehyde decreases with evolutionary stage, but higher sensitivity observations are needed

claims.hypothesis: Are HDCO and D2CO formed mainly on grain surfaces rather than in the gas phase?
claims.experiment: Compared column density ratios and the Rodgers & Charnley F parameter with models
claims.result: F between 0.1 and 1.1 (lower limits 0.1-0.6); D2CO/HDCO ~0.2 constant
claims.finding: Values cannot be explained by gas-phase chemistry and favour grain-surface chemistry, with some gas-phase contribution at the warm HMPO stage

evidence.quote: These values cannot be explained by gas phase chemistry, but are more consistent with grain surface chemistry models.
higher sensitivity observations are needed to provide more stringent constraints to the column density ratio of HDCO/D$_2$CO during the HMSC phase

claims.hypothesis: Do HMSCs show a different deuteration than HMPOs?
claims.experiment: Searched for HDCO and D2CO in three HMSCs and set 3 sigma upper limits
claims.finding: The trend between HMSC and HMPO phases cannot be constrained

evidence.quote: so we cannot constrain the trend between HMSC and HMPO phases

claims.hypothesis: What are the sizes of the H2CO-emitting regions?
claims.experiment: ALMA Band 6 213 GHz continuum 2D Gaussian fits and H2(13)CO contours
claims.finding: H2(13)CO emitting regions are similar to the continuum source sizes

evidence.quote: The H$_2^{13}$CO emitting regions are similar to the continuum source sizes

referee_caveats_inferred: Main results come from 34 arcsec APEX beams with an assumed 3-6 arcsec source size; ratios depend on this filling assumption and on the single-Tex LTE model
ALMA data play only a minor role and no ALMA reduction detail is given, so ALMA-derived sizes cannot be reproduced
Per-source results are tabulated with multiple velocity components and large scatter (e.g. 18517+0437), weakening the evolutionary-trend claim
HMSC sample has only upper limits, so the earliest-stage behaviour is unconstrained
Excitation temperature choice (HDCO versus H2CO lines) changes by factor 2-3 for bright sources

missing_for_reproduction: ALMA calibration and imaging recipe and parameters
Fit parameters and initial conditions for the MADCUBA fits and per-source source sizes
Reduced APEX and IRAM spectra and the exact line windows used
reproducibility.estimated_data_volume_inferred: ALMA ACA Band 6 for 8 pointings: small, likely a few GB raw; APEX/IRAM spectra negligible
reproducibility.score_reason: ALMA project code is given, but ALMA processing, imaging and size fits are not described; the main analysis uses APEX/IRAM spectra and MADCUBA fits with several unstated choices, although the final ratio tables are numeric.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: The paper does not state data availability, and the ALMA reduction recipe and fit settings are missing; the key results rest on single-dish data and an under-specified LTE fit.
